correctness.rationale: Exact 4x256 dynamic program enumerates all words by last-two-bit state and full three-mer support mask, preserving totals \(2^n\); gives unique full-mask maximum at each \(14\le n\le50\), \(n=13\) counterexample 989 vs 934, \(n=14\) gap 2632 vs 2218. Independent exhaustive word enumeration through 18 and inclusion-exclusion calculations corroborate. For \(n\ge51\), a missing triple prevents occurrence in \(\lfloor n/3\rfloor\) disjoint independent blocks; every proper fiber is bounded by \(2^n(7/8)^t\) and full fiber is at least \(2^n(1-8(7/8)^t)\), with strict difference because \(9(7/8)^{17}<1\). The exact all-length count follows from 4x4 forbidden-edge transfer matrices and inclusion-exclusion; no infinite conclusion is based on experiments.

originality.rationale: Closest full primary work on identical set-valued length-k substring spectra (Bernardini et al., DOI 10.1007/s00224-025-10240-z, Sections 1,2,5,7) solves a different optimization: list z shortest equivalent representatives for a GIVEN support, not identify the most populous support at a FIXED word length. Its general counting difficulty does not imply a modal cutoff. Full texts on k-abelian equivalence (arXiv:1605.03319), multiset substring spectra (arXiv:1912.11108), and substring-composition multisets (arXiv:1403.2439) preserve different data and do not imply this statement. Explicit title/alias/equivalence and numerical searches did not reveal the threshold. This is a qualified finding, not a proof of global priority; a few plausible historical full texts were not inspected.
residual_risks: The complete Skiena–Sundaram (1995) text was not accessible; a specialized combinatorial example outside its abstract could conceivably cover the \(n=14\) claim.
The 1975 Hutchinson/Wilf adjacency enumeration and Hutchinson overlap-sequence works were not inspected fully; an unindexed exact presence-only tabulation may exist.
The 2002 Pe’er–Arbili–Shamir full text could not be materially read, although its abstract describes a different reconstruction goal.
Web/indexed searches cannot establish global priority or coverage of unpublished research.

value.rationale: Exact worst-case ambiguity in a complete binary three-mer presence-only measurement is a natural reconstruction benchmark in sequencing-by-hybridization and existential string indexing. Before the sharp transition, all-probe-positive is NOT most ambiguous (\(n=13\): 934 vs 989); for every \(n\ge14\), full support uniquely is. The 256-matrix exact formula and universal threshold give reusable structural information beyond a numerical table. The closest same-set paper presents the general counting problem as distinct from multiset Euler-trail enumeration, supporting motivation for this tightly scoped tractable case. No general k-mer theorem is claimed.
